title: Differential onboarding grants and triggered CTA flow test
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: increase PLG conversion velocity (free -> paid) and early retention by testing a matrix of onboarding credit grant sizes, replenishment policies, expiration windows, and in-product upgrade prompts. Hypothesis: aligning grant cadence to early-product engagement patterns (first 7 days) and using contextual CTAs tied to high-value actions will increase 14-day paid conversion and reduce churn compared to the current one-time lump-sum grant.
experiment_arms: Arm A: One-time large grant (1000 tokens) expiring in 30 days with standard billing CTA
Arm B: Small recurring micro-grants (4 x 300 tokens weekly) with contextual CTAs after usage milestones
Arm C: Replenishing buffer (initial 500 tokens + 200 tokens on high-value events) with soft-expiry (tokens marked stale after 60 days but usable if triggered by retention event)
Arm D: No-expiry smaller grant (600 tokens) paired with in-product step-up modal after second high-intent request
upgrade_prompt_variants: Inline contextual CTA (banner near generation results) with one-click purchase link
Modal after high-value action (e.g., long completion generated) with quota visualization
Email + in-console reminder 48 hours before expiry
Progress bar in console header indicating % of onboarding grant consumed and conversion CTA
success_metrics: Secondary: Activation (first successful generation within 24h), 14-day retention, average tokens used in first 7 days, CAC payback velocity
Safety: fraud/abuse signal (multiple signups from same IP), promo exploitation rate
implementation_notes:
- Implement feature flaggable grant engine with arm selector.
- Instrument events: onboarding_grant_assigned, onboarding_grant_consumed, upgrade_prompt_shown, upgrade_clicked, payment_completed.
- Backend: new grant table indexed by account_id + grant_type; idempotency on assignment.
- Frontend: in-console banners and modal variants; email template for expiry reminders.
- Analytics: cohort dashboard (BigQuery) and conversion funnel in Looker; ensure attribution for multi-arm cohorts.
- Rollout: start with 5% traffic per arm, monitor abuse signals, scale to 25% if no red flags.
- Guardrails: single active onboarding grant per account; blocked for known test accounts and internal signups.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Grants increase short-term usage costs without lift in paid conversion — mitigation: cap total free tokens per org and pause high-cost arms if conversion < threshold after N days.
Risk: Fraud / multi-account exploitation — mitigation: throttle by device fingerprinting and require email/phone verification for large grants.
Risk: Enterprise sales confusion with variable grants — mitigation: surface enterprise-only flag to disable experimental grants for accounts flagged as enterprise during signup.
Risk: Tracking gaps between front-end prompts and billing conversion — mitigation: end-to-end instrumentation and conversion reconciliation weekly during experiment.
